chunks: And it was narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿImrān that he said:
I wrote to Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام concerning the squirrel fur, the mink, and the khazz, and I said: May I be your ransom, I would like that you not answer me with taqiyyah regarding that.
So he wrote to me in his own handwriting: “Pray in them.”

key_terms.الْخَزِّ: khazz, a type of fabric mentioned in legal discussions of prayer garments
key_terms.بِالتَّقِيَّةِ: with taqiyyah; dissimulative precaution due to circumstances
key_terms.فِيهَا: in them, referring to those garments

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat in garments made from squirrel, mink, and khazz according to Imam al-Jawad عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written question to Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام about the permissibility of praying in garments made from certain animal furs and khazz. The Imam عليه السلام replied in his own handwriting with a direct legal ruling permitting prayer in them, making the report relevant to prayer rulings and lawful garments.
